title: Continuous Functional Calculus for Self Adjoint and Normal Operators

items.title: Bounded Hilbert operators form a C star algebra
items.strategy: For nonzero complex Hilbert H, B(H) is complete with submultiplicative operator norm, identity of norm one and conjugate-linear isometric adjoint. Prove ||T*T||=||T||^2: one inequality is submultiplicativity, the other follows from ||Tx||^2=<T*Tx,x> <= ||T*T|| ||x||^2. This supplies the C*-hypotheses before the normal spectral-radius or generated-algebra arguments.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For every nonzero complex Hilbert space H, B(H), with the operator norm, composition, identity, and Hilbert adjoint, is a unital C-star algebra and ||T* T||=||T||^2.
items.axiom_audit: Uses Countable Choice through the Hilbert adjoint/orthogonal-decomposition suppliers and declares def-countable-choice; no full AC is used.

items.title: Spectrum of a self adjoint operator is real
items.strategy: For bounded self-adjoint T on nonzero complex H and Im z!=0, ||(T-z)x||>=|Im z| ||x||. Range is closed by completeness, dense by ker(T-conj z)=0 and adjoint orthogonality; hence onto with bounded inverse. Inner product linear in first argument.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. If T is a bounded self-adjoint operator on a nonzero complex Hilbert space, then sigma(T) is contained in R, and ||(T-zI)x|| >= |Im z| ||x|| for z outside R.
items.axiom_audit: Uses Countable Choice through the Hilbert adjoint/orthogonal-decomposition suppliers and declares def-countable-choice; no full AC is used.

items.title: Spectrum of a positive operator is nonnegative
items.strategy: For positive self-adjoint T and real t<0, <(T-t)x,x>>=|t| ||x||^2, hence bounded below; the same closed/dense range argument gives invertibility. Combine with real spectrum. This direction does not assume square roots.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. If T is a bounded positive operator, then sigma(T) is contained in [0,infinity).
items.axiom_audit: Uses Countable Choice through the Hilbert adjoint/orthogonal-decomposition suppliers and declares def-countable-choice; no full AC is used.

items.title: Order on bounded self adjoint operators
items.strategy: Define S<=T iff <(T-S)x,x>>=0 for all x. Check reflexivity and transitivity; antisymmetry uses polarization. Positivity/order is on the real vector space of bounded self-adjoint operators, not arbitrary operators.
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For bounded self-adjoint S,T define S<=T exactly when <(T-S)x,x>>=0 for every x; this is a partial order on the real vector space of bounded self-adjoint operators.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Uses Countable Choice through the Hilbert adjoint/orthogonal-decomposition suppliers and declares def-countable-choice; no full AC is used.

items.title: C star algebra generated by a normal operator
items.strategy: Define C*(I,T) as the norm closure of the complex *-algebra generated by I,T,T*. It is commutative iff T is normal: verify polynomial commutation and pass limits; converse reads TT*=T*T. Nonzero H for the unital nonempty-spectrum convention.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For T in B(H), C*(I,T) is the norm closure of the unital star algebra generated by T; it is commutative exactly when T is normal.
items.axiom_audit: Uses Countable Choice through the Hilbert adjoint/orthogonal-decomposition suppliers and declares def-countable-choice; no full AC is used.

items.title: Normal operator norm equals spectral radius
items.strategy: Apply the general C*-identity result to B(H); recover ||T||=max_sigma(T)|z| from normal calculus as a consistency check.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume AC. For a bounded normal operator T on a nonzero complex Hilbert space, ||T||=r(T)=max{|lambda|:lambda in sigma(T)}.
items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC through the C-star spectral-radius/Gelfand route and declares def-axiom-of-choice; no weaker branch is collapsed.

items.title: Normal operator with zero spectrum is zero
items.strategy: On nonzero complex H, normal T with sigma(T)={0} has norm zero. Non-normal nilpotents are reserved for the counterexample.
items.statement: Assume AC. A bounded normal operator whose spectrum is {0} is the zero operator.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC through the C-star spectral-radius/Gelfand route and declares def-axiom-of-choice; no weaker branch is collapsed.

items.title: Isometry coisometry and partial isometry
items.strategy: Define isometry by U*U=I, coisometry by UU*=I, partial isometry as zero on its kernel and isometric on its orthogonal complement. Initial space (ker U)^perp and final space ran U (closed for a partial isometry). Zero operator is a partial isometry.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. An operator U is an isometry if U*U=I, a coisometry if UU*=I, and a partial isometry if it vanishes on ker U and is isometric on (ker U)^perp; these are its initial and final-space conventions.
items.axiom_audit: Uses Countable Choice through the Hilbert adjoint/orthogonal-decomposition suppliers and declares def-countable-choice; no full AC is used.

items.title: Partial isometry characterizations
items.strategy: Equivalence of the partial-isometry definition, U*U being the orthogonal projection onto (ker U)^perp, and UU* being the projection onto ran U. Prove the adjoint version and closedness of range; neither projection is assumed to be I. Define the orthogonal projection onto a closed Hilbert subspace inline from its orthogonal decomposition; the published def-orthogonal-projection is finite-dimensional and is inadequate here.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For bounded U, the partial-isometry condition is equivalent to U*U being the orthogonal projection onto (ker U)^perp, and then UU* is the orthogonal projection onto ran U; equivalently U* is a partial isometry.
items.axiom_audit: Uses Countable Choice through the Hilbert adjoint/orthogonal-decomposition suppliers and declares def-countable-choice; no full AC is used.

items.title: Numerical range and numerical radius
items.strategy: On nonzero complex H with inner product linear in its first variable define W(T)={<Tx,x>:||x||=1}, w(T)=sup|W(T)|. For H=0 set w(0)=0 separately; do not silently take max of an empty spectrum.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: For bounded T on a nonzero complex Hilbert space, W(T)={<Tx,x>:||x||=1} and w(T)=sup{|z|:z in W(T)}; set w(0)=0 on the zero space.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free relative to the displayed Hilbert-space/operator data; no selection or maximality principle is used.

items.title: Numerical radius is an equivalent operator norm
items.strategy: Complex polarization of the bounded sesquilinear form gives ||T||<=2w(T), while w(T)<=||T|| is Cauchy-Schwarz; prove triangle inequality, homogeneity and definiteness. For normal T show each spectral value is an approximate eigenvalue: normality equates kernel norms of T-lambda and its adjoint, so bounded below would give a bounded inverse. Thus sigma(T) lies in closure W(T), yielding equality. A real skew-symmetric nonzero matrix has zero quadratic form, so do not state the estimate over R.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume AC. On a complex Hilbert space, w is a norm with w(T)<=||T||<=2w(T); if T is normal, w(T)=||T||.
items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC through the C-star spectral-radius/Gelfand route and declares def-axiom-of-choice; no weaker branch is collapsed.

items.title: Polynomial calculus is isometric for self adjoint operators
items.strategy: Verify B(H) is a unital C*-algebra from ||T*T||=||T||^2, using Cauchy-Schwarz and the Hilbert adjoint. For self-adjoint T, p(T) is normal and ||p(T)||=max_sigma(T)|p| by polynomial spectral mapping and normal spectral radius. Thus restriction classes of polynomials are well-defined and isometric.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume AC. If T=T* and p is a complex polynomial, then ||p(T)||=max_{lambda in sigma(T)}|p(lambda)|; hence polynomial restriction classes on sigma(T) give a well-defined isometric calculus.
items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC through the C-star spectral-radius/Gelfand route and declares def-axiom-of-choice; no weaker branch is collapsed.

items.title: Continuous functional calculus for bounded self adjoint operators
items.strategy: For bounded self-adjoint T on nonzero complex H, restrict complex polynomials to its compact real spectrum; constants and coordinate separate, conjugation stays polynomial. Extend the polynomial isometry uniquely by uniform density and completeness into B(H). Product and adjoint pass to limits; range is C*(I,T). Establish uniqueness among continuous unital *-homomorphisms, then prove automatic contractivity if the unrestricted formulation is used. No square root or Borel calculus in construction.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume AC. For bounded self-adjoint T there is a unique isometric unital star homomorphism C(sigma(T))->B(H), f↦f(T), sending the coordinate function to T, with range C*(I,T).
items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC through the C-star spectral-radius/Gelfand route and declares def-axiom-of-choice; no weaker branch is collapsed.

items.title: Spectral permanence for unital c star subalgebras
items.strategy: For unital C*-subalgebra B of A with the same identity, invertibility in A implies inverse in B. For invertible self-adjoint x in B, C*(I,x,x^-1) is commutative; in its Gelfand image x separates characters since its reciprocal determines x^-1. Stone-Weierstrass gives x^-1 in C*(I,x). For general x apply this to x*x and xx*, obtaining both left and right inverses. This is Williams Theorem 4.8 and precedes any normal continuous calculus.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume AC. If B is a unital C-star subalgebra of a unital C-star algebra A with the same identity, then sigma_B(b)=sigma_A(b) for every b in B.
items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC through the C-star spectral-radius/Gelfand route and declares def-axiom-of-choice; no weaker branch is collapsed.

items.title: Character space of generated normal algebra is operator spectrum
items.strategy: For normal T, chi->chi(T) maps Delta(C*(I,T)) onto sigma_B(H)(T) by character spectrum and permanence. It is injective because chi(T*)=conj chi(T) and *-polynomials are dense. Compact-to-Hausdorff gives homeomorphism.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume AC. For normal T, chi↦chi(T) is a homeomorphism from the character space of C*(I,T) onto the operator spectrum sigma(T).
items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC through the C-star spectral-radius/Gelfand route and declares def-axiom-of-choice; no weaker branch is collapsed.

items.title: Continuous functional calculus for bounded normal operators
items.strategy: Compose pullback by chi->chi(T) with inverse Gelfand to obtain C(sigma(T)) onto C*(I,T), isometric unital *-isomorphism sending z to T. Uniqueness uses density of polynomials in z and conjugate z, not holomorphic polynomials alone; agrees with the earlier self-adjoint construction.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume AC. For bounded normal T there is a unique isometric unital star isomorphism C(sigma(T))->C*(I,T), f↦f(T), sending z to T; for self-adjoint T it agrees with the preceding calculus.
items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC through the C-star spectral-radius/Gelfand route and declares def-axiom-of-choice; no weaker branch is collapsed.

items.title: Spectral mapping for continuous normal functional calculus
items.strategy: For continuous complex f, f(T) is normal and sigma_B(H)(f(T))=f(sigma(T)): pointwise invertibility in C(sigma T), transported isomorphism, then permanence. This includes constant functions and disconnected spectra.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume AC. If T is bounded normal and f is continuous on sigma(T), then f(T) is normal and sigma(f(T))=f(sigma(T)).
items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC through the C-star spectral-radius/Gelfand route and declares def-axiom-of-choice; no weaker branch is collapsed.

items.title: Continuous functional calculus properties
items.strategy: Prove norm identity, linearity, multiplicativity, conjugation and uniform convergence from the star isomorphism. For f>=0 write f=g-bar*g with g=sqrt(f), so positivity uses quadratic forms without an operator square-root theorem; conversely positive f(T) has nonnegative spectrum by the earlier lemma. For continuous g on f(sigma T), prove g(f(T))=(g composed f)(T) first for star polynomials and then uniformly. Prove the eigenvector identity by polynomial approximation in the self-adjoint case and star-polynomial approximation in the normal case, first deriving T*x=conjugate(lambda)x. Operators commuting with both T and T* commute with every approximant and hence every f(T); for self-adjoint T, commuting with T suffices. No holomorphic or Borel calculus is invoked.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume AC. The normal continuous calculus preserves sums, products, conjugation and positivity, is norm-continuous, obeys continuous composition, sends eigenvectors at lambda to scalar evaluation at lambda, and commutes with every S satisfying ST=TS and ST*=T*S.
items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC through the C-star spectral-radius/Gelfand route and declares def-axiom-of-choice; no weaker branch is collapsed.

items.title: Self adjoint norm and spectrum extrema
items.strategy: For nonzero H and self-adjoint T let m=min sigma(T), M=max sigma(T). Spectral positivity via calculus gives mI<=T<=MI. Conversely any quadratic lower/upper bound lies below/above spectral extrema by the resolvent lemma for positive shifts. Hence inf/sup unit-vector quadratic forms are m,M, and ||T||=max(|m|,|M|). Suprema need not be attained by vectors.
items.statement: Assume AC. If T=T*, then min sigma(T) I <= T <= max sigma(T) I, these bounds are sharp, and ||T||=max{|min sigma(T)|,|max sigma(T)|}.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC through the C-star spectral-radius/Gelfand route and declares def-axiom-of-choice; no weaker branch is collapsed.

items.title: Positive square root
items.strategy: For bounded positive T, define S=sqrt(id)(T) by uniform polynomial approximation on [0,||T||]. Its positivity follows from the scalar fourth-root factorization; S^2=T. Any R>=0 with R^2=T commutes with T and thus S; in C*(I,R,S), characters of R,S are nonnegative by spectral permanence, so equality of squares forces equality. Every bounded operator commuting with T commutes with polynomial approximants and S. Do not use Borel calculus.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume AC. Every bounded positive T has a unique bounded positive square root T^(1/2); it belongs to C*(I,T), commutes with every operator commuting with T, and is obtained by continuous polynomial approximation on sigma(T), without Borel calculus.
items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC through the C-star spectral-radius/Gelfand route and declares def-axiom-of-choice; no weaker branch is collapsed.

items.title: Absolute value of a bounded operator
items.strategy: Define |T|=(T*T)^(1/2); |||T|x||=||Tx|| and ker|T|=ker T follow from the squared quadratic norm. Reconcile FA-16's compact special case by uniqueness, without depending on a B example.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume AC. For bounded T define |T|=(T*T)^(1/2), a positive operator with ker|T|=ker T and |||T|x||=||Tx||.
items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC through the C-star spectral-radius/Gelfand route and declares def-axiom-of-choice; no weaker branch is collapsed.

items.title: Polar decomposition for bounded operators
items.strategy: Define U(|T|x)=Tx on ran |T|, well-defined and isometric by equal norms. Extend uniquely to its closure and set zero on ker T. Then T=U|T|, ker U=ker T, initial closure ran |T|, final closure ran T. Uniqueness requires the kernel/support convention; T=0 alone would not determine arbitrary factors.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume AC. Every bounded T has a unique partial isometry U with T=U|T| and ker U=ker T; its initial space is closure ran|T| and its final space is closure ran T.
items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC through the C-star spectral-radius/Gelfand route and declares def-axiom-of-choice; no weaker branch is collapsed.

items.title: Bounded normal operator abstract spectral theorem
items.strategy: Package the proved isomorphism as the abstract spectral theorem: C*(I,T) is C(sigma T), with T represented by the coordinate function. Do not assert a projection-valued measure, Borel calculus, or a multiplication representation of H; those are FA-20.
items.statement: Assume AC. A bounded operator is normal exactly when it is the image of the coordinate function under a unital star representation of C(K) for some compact K; canonically K=sigma(T) and the representation is the continuous functional calculus.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC through the C-star spectral-radius/Gelfand route and declares def-axiom-of-choice; no weaker branch is collapsed.

items.title: Positive square root and covariance matrices
items.strategy: Orientation for PT-9: finite-dimensional positive semidefinite covariance matrices use this unique positive square root. PT-9 must supply positivity of covariance; no probability theorem is proved here.
items.statement: Assume AC. For a finite-dimensional positive covariance matrix C, the unique positive square root C^(1/2) is obtained by the same continuous calculus and transforms under unitary coordinate change as (UCU*)^(1/2)=UC^(1/2)U*.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Uses full AC only through the positive-square-root supplier and declares def-axiom-of-choice; the finite-dimensional covariance calculation introduces no further choice.

items.title: Two dimensional numerical range is convex
items.strategy: For a complex 2x2 matrix write rank-one orthogonal projections as (I+r.sigma)/2 with r in the real unit sphere S^2; verify the coordinates directly (diagonal entries (1+z)/2,(1-z)/2). W is an affine real-linear image of S^2 in R^2. Since the linear map has nontrivial kernel, its image of S^2 equals its image of the closed unit ball, which is convex. One-dimensional compressions give singletons.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. The numerical range of the compression of an operator to any complex subspace of dimension at most two is convex.
items.axiom_audit: Uses Countable Choice through the Hilbert adjoint/orthogonal-decomposition suppliers and declares def-countable-choice; no full AC is used.

items.title: Toeplitz hausdorff
items.strategy: Given two unit vectors, compress T to their complex span (dimension <=2). Both numerical values and their segment belong to the compression numerical range and hence W(T). No closure is inserted in this argument. Example M_t on L2[0,1] has W=(0,1), so numerical range need not be closed.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. The numerical range W(T) of every bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space is convex.

title: Continuous Functional Calculus for Self Adjoint and Normal Operators — Examples

items.title: Functional calculus for a diagonal operator
items.strategy: For bounded complex sequence lambda_n on ell2(N), T e_n=lambda_n e_n. Prove spectrum equals closure{lambda_n} by the bounded reciprocal diagonal inverse and approximate basis eigenvectors. Then f(T)e_n=f(lambda_n)e_n by *-polynomial approximation.
items.statement: Assume AC. For a bounded diagonal operator Te_n=lambda_n e_n on ell^2(N), sigma(T)=closure{lambda_n} and f(T)e_n=f(lambda_n)e_n for every continuous f on sigma(T).

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis

items.axiom_audit: Inherits the explicit choice strength of the cited A-page suppliers; the concrete calculation introduces no stronger choice principle.

items.title: Functional calculus for a multiplication operator
items.strategy: On L2([0,1],Lebesgue), T=M_t has spectrum [0,1]: reciprocal multiplication outside, normalized interval indicators near each lambda inside. Polynomial calculus then uniform approximation yields f(T)=M_f. Verify norm equals sup for continuous f by positive measure neighborhoods.
items.statement: Assume AC. For T=M_t on L^2([0,1]), sigma(T)=[0,1] and f(T)=M_f for every continuous f on [0,1].

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis

items.title: Square root and absolute value of a matrix
items.strategy: For T=[[0,2],[0,0]], T*T=diag(0,4), hence |T|=diag(0,2); also compute sqrt(diag(1,4))=diag(1,2), verify positivity and uniqueness through the theorem.
items.statement: Assume AC. For T=[[0,2],[0,0]], |T|=diag(0,2); in particular the positive square root of diag(1,4) is diag(1,2).

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis

items.title: Polar decomposition of the unilateral shift
items.strategy: On ell2(N0), Se_n=e_(n+1), S*S=I, SS*=I-P_e0. Thus |S|=I and its polar partial isometry is S, initial all H, final e0-perp. It is an isometry, not a unitary.
items.statement: Assume AC. For the unilateral shift S on ell^2(N_0), |S|=I and S itself is the polar partial isometry, with initial space H and final space e_0^perp.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis

items.title: A quasinilpotent operator need not be zero
items.strategy: Use nonzero 2x2 Jordan nilpotent J, J^2=0. Compute spectrum {0} directly and JJ*!=J*J; this disproves dropping normality.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis

items.statement: Assume AC. The nonzero nilpotent matrix [[0,1],[0,0]] has spectrum {0} but is not normal, so the normality hypothesis in the zero-spectrum corollary is necessary.
items.axiom_audit: Inherits the explicit choice strength of the cited A-page suppliers; the concrete calculation introduces no stronger choice principle.

items.title: Continuous calculus does not contain discontinuous spectral projections
items.strategy: On L2[0,1], P=M_indicator_[0,1/2] is an orthogonal projection commuting with M_t. If P=f(M_t) with f continuous on [0,1], equality of multipliers a.e. forces f=1 on (0,1/2) and f=0 on (1/2,1), contradicting continuity. No PVM existence theorem is used; the concrete projection only motivates FA-20.
items.statement: Assume AC. For T=M_t on L^2([0,1]), the commuting projection M_{1_[0,1/2]} does not equal f(T) for any continuous f on [0,1].

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis

items.title: Self adjointness cannot be dropped from the order calculus
items.strategy: The Jordan nilpotent [[0,1],[0,0]] has nonnegative real spectrum {0}, but <Jx,x> is nonreal for x=(1,i)/sqrt(2) under the first-linear convention. Thus nonnegative spectrum alone does not imply positivity without self-adjointness; this is the exact claim refuted.
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. The Jordan nilpotent J=[[0,1],[0,0]] has nonnegative real spectrum {0} but is not positive; thus spectral nonnegativity does not characterize positivity without self-adjointness.

title: Spectral Measures and Borel Functional Calculus

items.title: Projection valued measure
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. On a measurable space (X,Σ), a PVM E takes values in orthogonal projections on a complex Hilbert space H, satisfies E(∅)=0, E(X)=I, E(B∩C)=E(B)E(C), and E(∪B_n)x=Σ E(B_n)x in norm for pairwise disjoint B_n. Regular on a locally compact space means each finite positive scalar measure E_x is regular. Inner products are linear in the first variable. Here orthogonal projection means a bounded operator P with P²=P=P*, with no finite-dimensional restriction.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Uses Countable Choice only through the Hilbert adjoint/projection infrastructure and declares def-countable-choice; no full AC or maximality argument is used.
items.strategy: This fixes the infinite-dimensional convention used throughout the page. A bounded idempotent P with P=P* is the orthogonal projection onto its closed range by the inspected Hilbert adjoint and orthogonal-decomposition interfaces. Strong countable additivity is part of the definition; the next lemma proves its equivalent weak formulation. For x in H, E_x(B)=<E(B)x,x> is finite and positive because E(B) is a contractive orthogonal projection, so the regularity clause is meaningful.

items.title: Weak and strong additivity of orthogonal projections
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For orthogonal projection values multiplicative on intersections, weak countable additivity and strong countable additivity are equivalent.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Uses Countable Choice only through the Hilbert adjoint/projection infrastructure and declares def-countable-choice; no full AC or maximality argument is used.
items.strategy: For disjoint B_n, partial sums P_N are orthogonal projections below E(∪B_n); the squared norm of (E(∪B_n)-P_N)x equals its quadratic pairing with x, which tends to zero by weak additivity. Strong implies weak by Cauchy–Schwarz.

items.title: Scalar and complex measures from a pvm
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. E_x(B)=〈E(B)x,x〉 is positive finite with mass ||x||²; E_{x,y}(B)=〈E(B)x,y〉 is a finite complex measure, linear in x, conjugate-linear in y. Its variation is at most ||x||||y||.

Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Uses Countable Choice only through the Hilbert adjoint/projection infrastructure and declares def-countable-choice; no full AC or maximality argument is used.
items.strategy: Polarize quadratic measures using E_{x,y}=1/4 Σ_{k=0}^3 i^k E_{x+i^k y}. For each finite disjoint partition use Cauchy–Schwarz twice to bound Σ|〈E(B_j)x,y〉| by ||x||||y||.

items.title: Integral of a simple function against a pvm
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For a finite disjoint measurable partition and s=Σ a_j 1_{B_j}, define ∫s dE=Σ a_j E(B_j). Include the zero-coefficient complement.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Uses Countable Choice only through the Hilbert adjoint/projection infrastructure and declares def-countable-choice; no full AC or maximality argument is used.
items.strategy: To prove independence of the displayed representation, adjoin the zero-coefficient complement to each finite partition and refine two representations by all intersections B_j intersect C_k. The PVM identity E(B_j intersect C_k)=E(B_j)E(C_k), finite additivity, and equality of the two scalar values on each nonempty refinement cell give the same operator sum. Thus the definition depends only on the simple function, not its chosen partition.

items.title: Simple pvm integral is representation independent
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. The simple integral is independent of its disjoint presentation, satisfies 〈(∫s dE)x,y〉=∫s dE_{x,y}, and ||(∫s dE)x||²=∫|s|² dE_x.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Uses Countable Choice only through the Hilbert adjoint/projection infrastructure and declares def-countable-choice; no full AC or maximality argument is used.
items.strategy: Refine two partitions by all intersections; use orthogonality. Its norm is the maximum of |a_j| over nonzero projections, with zero for the zero operator.

items.title: Bounded borel pvm integral
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Every bounded measurable complex f has a unique integral Φ_E(f), obtained from uniform simple approximations. It satisfies ||Φ_E(f)||≤||f||∞, the scalar pairing identity and ||Φ_E(f)x||²=∫|f|² dE_x. The exact norm is the E-essential supremum.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Uses Countable Choice only through the Hilbert adjoint/projection infrastructure and declares def-countable-choice; no full AC or maximality argument is used.
items.strategy: Approximate the bounded complex range by finite grids, prove the operators are norm Cauchy and the limit independent; pass the simple identities to limits. For the reverse essential-norm inequality use a nonzero spectral projection on {|f|>c}.

items.title: Pvm integral is a star homomorphism
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Φ_E is a unital star homomorphism. If f_n→f pointwise E-almost everywhere and sup_n||f_n||∞<∞, then Φ_E(f_n)→Φ_E(f) strongly.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Uses Countable Choice only through the Hilbert adjoint/projection infrastructure and declares def-countable-choice; no full AC or maximality argument is used.
items.strategy: First multiply simple functions on a common partition; uniform approximation proves products and adjoints. Apply scalar dominated convergence to ∫|f_n-f|² dE_x.

items.title: Continuous functional calculus produces a regular PVM
items.statement: Assume AC. For compact K and a unital star representation pi:C(K)->B(H), there is a unique regular PVM E with pi(f)=integral f dE for every continuous f.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC through the normal continuous calculus and spectral representation suppliers; any additional Zorn use is identified in the strategy and def-axiom-of-choice is declared.
items.strategy: For each x, Riesz–Markov represents the positive functional f↦<pi(f)x,x> by a finite regular measure mu_x. Polarize with the fixed first-variable-linear convention and use scalar uniqueness to obtain bounded sesquilinear complex measures mu_xy; Hilbert Riesz then defines a bounded operator Psi(g) by <Psi(g)x,y>=integral g dmu_xy for every bounded Borel g. Psi extends pi and respects adjoints. From pi(fg)=pi(f)pi(g) for continuous f,g, uniqueness of representing measures first upgrades one multiplier and then the other from continuous to Borel, proving Psi(fg)=Psi(f)Psi(g) without assuming a PVM. Now E(B)=Psi(1_B) is self-adjoint idempotent, intersections multiply, and scalar countable additivity plus the weak/strong lemma gives SOT additivity. Only after E is proved a PVM identify Psi with its PVM integral. Uniqueness follows from all scalar pairings and Riesz–Markov uniqueness.

items.title: Spectral theorem for bounded normal operators pvm form
items.statement: Assume AC. Every bounded normal T on H has a unique regular PVM on σ(T) with T=∫z dE(z). Conversely such an integral is normal.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC through the normal continuous calculus and spectral representation suppliers; any additional Zorn use is identified in the strategy and def-axiom-of-choice is declared.
items.strategy: Apply the preceding representation theorem to the normal continuous calculus on K=sigma(T), so the coordinate function integrates to T. If F is another compactly supported PVM with the same coordinate integral, its PVM integral is a unital star representation of C(K) sending z to T; uniqueness of the normal continuous calculus makes all continuous scalar pairings agree, and Riesz–Markov uniqueness makes E=F. Conversely the PVM star-homomorphism sends z to a normal operator.

items.title: Borel functional calculus for a bounded normal operator
items.statement: Assume AC. For bounded normal T and bounded Borel f on σ(T), define f(T)=Φ_E(f) using its unique regular spectral PVM.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC through the normal continuous calculus and spectral representation suppliers; any additional Zorn use is identified in the strategy and def-axiom-of-choice is declared.
items.strategy: Well-definedness follows from the preceding spectral theorem's uniqueness of the regular PVM E and the previously constructed bounded-Borel PVM integral Phi_E. Restricting to bounded Borel functions ensures Phi_E(f) is a bounded operator. The following theorem proves the algebraic, norm, convergence, and compatibility properties; none is silently built into this definition.

items.title: Borel functional calculus for bounded normal operators
items.statement: Assume AC. The bounded Borel calculus extends the continuous calculus, is a unital star homomorphism with E-essential-supremum norm, obeys bounded pointwise E-a.e. convergence in SOT, and every operator commuting with both T and T* commutes with all f(T).

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC through the normal continuous calculus and spectral representation suppliers; any additional Zorn use is identified in the strategy and def-axiom-of-choice is declared.
items.strategy: The representation lemma identifies continuous PVM integrals with the previous calculus; the general PVM integral gives algebra, adjoint, norm and convergence laws. For commutation, scalar uniqueness shows that an operator commuting with T and T* commutes with every spectral projection, then with simple integrals and their norm limits. Do not invoke Fuglede or assume commutation with T alone.

items.title: Spectral projections and resolution of the identity
items.statement: Assume AC. E(B)=1_B(T) reduces T; E({λ})H=ker(T-λ). For bounded self-adjoint T, F(t)=E((−∞,t]) is increasing, right SOT continuous, with strong limits 0 and I at the two infinities.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.strategy: Use integral multiplication and the norm-square identity; continuity follows from decreasing scalar measures and then quadratic norms.

items.title: Support and uniqueness of the spectral measure
items.statement: Assume AC. The support of the spectral PVM of bounded normal T is σ(T); it and all pairings are uniquely determined by T.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC through the normal continuous calculus and spectral representation suppliers; any additional Zorn use is identified in the strategy and def-axiom-of-choice is declared.
items.strategy: If a disk about lambda has zero projection, choose a nonzero continuous function supported in that disk; faithful isometry of the continuous calculus contradicts its zero integral. Hence support is sigma(T). Conversely outside the support the bounded reciprocal of z-lambda integrates to a two-sided inverse. Scalar Riesz–Markov uniqueness determines every pairing and polarization determines E. Treat the zero Hilbert space separately.

items.title: Cyclic vector and cyclic normal operator
items.statement: Assume AC. A vector x is cyclic when the closure of {f(T)x:f∈C(σ(T))} is H. For normal T this means the unital star algebra generated by T and T*, not only nonnegative powers of T. The same construction defines H_x for an arbitrary vector.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC through the normal continuous calculus and spectral representation suppliers; any additional Zorn use is identified in the strategy and def-axiom-of-choice is declared.
items.strategy: The normal continuous calculus identifies C(sigma(T)) with the norm-closed unital star algebra generated by T, so the displayed orbit has the same closure as the orbit under polynomials in T and T*. Hence H_x is unambiguously a closed cyclic subspace. The star-algebra description also makes H_x invariant under both T and T*, hence reducing; this is the property consumed by the cyclic decomposition below.

items.title: Cyclic spectral representation
items.statement: Assume AC. For cyclic x, f↦f(T)x extends to a unitary L²(σ(T),E_x)→H intertwining M_z with T and Borel multipliers with the Borel calculus. For arbitrary x its range is H_x.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem
John B. Conway, A Course in Functional Analysis, 2nd ed.

items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC through the normal continuous calculus and spectral representation suppliers; any additional Zorn use is identified in the strategy and def-axiom-of-choice is declared.
items.strategy: For continuous f, the PVM norm-square identity makes f↦f(T)x an isometry from C(sigma(T)) with its L²(E_x) norm. Radon L² density and L² completeness extend it uniquely to an isometry on L²; cyclicity makes its closed range all of H (or H_x for arbitrary x). The product law intertwines continuous multipliers. For bounded Borel g, approximate each L² vector by continuous functions and use ||g(T)y||<=||g||∞||y|| together with the Borel product law to pass to the limit, giving U M_g U^{-1}=g(T), in particular U M_z U^{-1}=T.

items.title: Maximal orthogonal family of cyclic reducing subspaces
items.statement: Assume AC. Every bounded normal operator admits a family of mutually orthogonal cyclic reducing subspaces whose Hilbert sum is H. General existence uses AC/Zorn; in separable H a given dense sequence constructs a finite or countable such family.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem

items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC through the normal continuous calculus and spectral representation suppliers; any additional Zorn use is identified in the strategy and def-axiom-of-choice is declared.
items.strategy: For x, the closed span of {p(T,T*)x} is invariant under T and T*, hence reducing and cyclic. Order pairwise orthogonal families of such nonzero subspaces by inclusion; unions bound chains, so Zorn (the unique full-AC step in the general decomposition) gives a maximal family. A nonzero vector in its reducing orthogonal complement would enlarge it. In separable H, alternatively project the first vector of a fixed dense sequence not already captured and obtain a finite or countable family.

items.title: Multiplication operator form of the bounded normal spectral theorem
items.statement: Assume AC. Every bounded normal T on an arbitrary complex Hilbert space is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by z on an orthogonal Hilbert sum direct_sum_j L^2(sigma(T),mu_j); in separable H the index set is finite or countable.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis
Dana P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem
John B. Conway, A Course in Functional Analysis, 2nd ed.

items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC through the normal continuous calculus and spectral representation suppliers; any additional Zorn use is identified in the strategy and def-axiom-of-choice is declared.
items.strategy: Apply the cyclic representation on every subspace of the maximal orthogonal family. Define the arbitrary Hilbert sum by square-summable coordinate families; each vector has at most countably many nonzero coordinates. The direct sum of cyclic unitaries is isometric on finite-support vectors, extends by completeness, is onto by maximality, and intertwines T coordinatewise.

items.title: Spectral multiplicity function in the separable case
items.statement: Assume AC. For nonzero separable H, choose a countable cyclic model with nonzero finite measures mu_j, put mu=sum_j 2^(-j)mu_j/(1+mu_j(C)), h_j=dmu_j/dmu and F_j={h_j>0}; the standard measurable fiber is span{e_k:1<=k<=m(z)} where m(z)=sum_j 1_{F_j}(z), after measurably enumerating active coordinates. The invariant is the scalar measure class together with this Borel fiber-dimension function, pending the independence theorem below; it is not point-eigenspace dimension away from atoms.

references.title: John B. Conway, A Course in Functional Analysis, 2nd ed.
Andreas Kriegl, Funktionalanalysis lecture notes

items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC through the normal continuous calculus and spectral representation suppliers; any additional Zorn use is identified in the strategy and def-axiom-of-choice is declared.
items.strategy: The weighted sum is a finite scalar spectral measure with exactly the common PVM-null sets. Radon–Nikodym square-root transport embeds each L^2(mu_j) as its active coordinate over mu; increasing-index enumeration of the active countable coordinates is measurable and produces the standard field with fiber dimension m(z). This defines a representative from one cyclic decomposition; the later intertwiner lemma proves independence.

items.title: Unitary intertwiners preserve direct-integral fiber dimension
items.statement: Assume AC. A unitary intertwining multiplication by z on two standard separable measurable-field models preserves their scalar measure class and their fiber dimensions almost everywhere; multiplicity is dim H_z, not dim ker(T-zI) at a non-atomic point.

references.title: John B. Conway, A Course in Functional Analysis, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Chapter IX §10, Propositions 10.17–10.20 and Theorem 10.21, pp.299–301; decomposability details completed locally

references.title: Andreas Kriegl, Funktionalanalysis lecture notes

items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC through the normal continuous calculus and spectral representation suppliers; any additional Zorn use is identified in the strategy and def-axiom-of-choice is declared.
items.strategy: Intertwining T and T* intertwines continuous functions; scalar Riesz–Markov uniqueness then intertwines every spectral projection. Thus zero projection sets agree, which identifies the two scalar measure classes. Use Radon–Nikodym square roots to put both models over one finite measure mu. The transported unitary U commutes with every scalar indicator multiplier. On a finite-measure exhaustion, apply U to the countable fundamental sections e_j 1_{m>=j}; the module identity U(1_B s)=1_B U(s), first for indicators and then bounded measurable scalars, defines measurable fiber columns v_j(z). Equality of integrals over every Borel B makes <v_j(z),v_k(z)>=delta_jk wherever j,k are active. Repeat the construction for U^{-1}; on one common conull set the two countable column matrices compose to the identity, so the fiber maps are onto as well as isometric. Therefore dim H_z=dim K_z a.e. This supplies the complete decomposability and dimension argument, including infinite countable fibers.

items.title: Unitary equivalence classified by measure class and multiplicity
items.statement: Assume AC. Two bounded normal operators on nonzero separable complex Hilbert spaces are unitarily equivalent iff their scalar spectral measure classes on C coincide and multiplicity functions coincide almost everywhere for that class. No change of spectral coordinate is allowed. The zero space is a separate trivial class.

references.title: John B. Conway, A Course in Functional Analysis, 2nd ed.
Andreas Kriegl, Funktionalanalysis lecture notes

items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC through the normal continuous calculus and spectral representation suppliers; any additional Zorn use is identified in the strategy and def-axiom-of-choice is declared.
items.strategy: Put each operator into the standard common-measure fiber model constructed above. Necessity is the full intertwiner lemma. Conversely, if the measure classes coincide, Radon–Nikodym square-root multiplication transports both models to one finite measure; equality m=n a.e. lets the canonical coordinate identity define a measurable fiberwise unitary, whose direct integral intertwines multiplication by z. Changes on null sets do not matter. The zero Hilbert space is handled as a separate trivial class.

items.title: Stone resolvent formula for spectral projections
items.statement: Assume AC. For bounded self-adjoint T and real a<b, (2πi)^(-1)∫_a^b[(T-(t+iε))^(-1)-(T-(t-iε))^(-1)]dt tends strongly as ε↓0 to E((a,b))+(E({a})+E({b}))/2.

references.title: Gerald Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 2nd ed.
Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis

items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC through the normal continuous calculus and spectral representation suppliers; any additional Zorn use is identified in the strategy and def-axiom-of-choice is declared.
items.strategy: For fixed epsilon the resolvent integrand is operator-norm continuous, so bounded linear scalar pairings commute with its Bochner integral. The scalar functional-calculus kernel is [arctan((b-lambda)/epsilon)-arctan((a-lambda)/epsilon)]/pi, lies in [0,1], and converges pointwise to 1_(a,b)+one half of the two endpoint indicators. Bounded Borel SOT convergence yields the stated strong limit. The resolvent convention is R_T(z)=(T-zI)^(-1), fixing the displayed sign.
